podcast.body: Released in 1967, this song is noted for sharing a similar guitar riff with Chicago's "25 or 6 to 4" (1970) and Green Day's "Brain Stew" (1995), illustrating that guitar riffs are not copyrightable. Its conception also occurred around the same time George Harrison wrote "While My Guitar Gently Weeps." "here's Babe I'm going to leave you from Led Zeppelin in 1967."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song, released in 1969, shares a guitar riff with The Beatles' "While My Guitar Gently Weeps," written around the same time, but is played at a different tempo. "And now here's Babe I'm going to leave you from Led Zeppelin in 1967. Which by the way was conceived around the same time that George Harrison wrote while my guitar gently weeps for the Beatles. Same riff, but different tempo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
